title: Exact derived normalization of the Etale comparison path
statement: For every commutative ring, chosen Cartesian square and bounded-below input, the Etale derived path equals the exact derived image of comparisonSquareEtalePath, precomposed with comparisonSquareSourceIso.inv and postcomposed with comparisonSquareTargetIso.hom. These paths and endpoint factors are the explicit constructions of [stage3-proetale-comparison-square-paths]. This asserts only one path identification; it assumes and concludes no square coherence. The square is supplied by an IsPullback proof. The assertion is HEq between the derived ordinary path composite and the stated component path, retaining their definitionally equal endpoint presentations to avoid expensive kernel conversion.

proof.text: Apply the proved exact-derived square-pasting identity to the two edge comparisons at f and g-prime. Naturality of mapDerivedCategoryCompIso in its first functor inserts the etale square whiskered by the comparison pullback. Cancel the endpoint composition factors. This gives exact_path, the three-factor normalization before replacing exact pro-etale pullbacks by total left derived functors.

Prove restriction_path for arbitrary exact functors: the fully faithful bounded-below inclusion sends the composite of two restricted composition comparisons and a middle transport to mapDerivedCategorySquareIso. Obtain the inverse comparison from equality of isomorphisms. For the scheme square, prove etale_square_expansion and plus_square_expansion as separate equations before evaluation at M; the latter uses Etale.pullbackSquareComparison_def and reflexivity. Equality induction proves plus_transport for the middle equality transport. Apply restriction_path, map the two expansion equations to components, and compose the three equalities to obtain square_restrict. Keeping plus_square_expansion separate prevents the kernel from repeatedly unfolding the bounded-below functor constructions.

Expand leftDerivedUpperStarComparisonIso: its bounded-below compatibility is the identity, leaving the exact-derived edge comparison followed by the inverse exactness isomorphism. In exact_path_with_comparisons apply naturality of the inverse exactness isomorphism at g-prime twice, to the edge comparison at f and to its endpoint exactness isomorphism. These give precisely the last factors of comparisonSquareTargetIso. Expand the source and target isomorphisms, evaluate at M.obj, and combine with the restriction identity for the etale square. No pro-etale square normalization or underived coherence hypothesis is used. The private exactOrdinaryPath, exactSourceIso, exactTargetIso and exactDerivedPath constructors retain the explicit parenthesizations of the public path definitions. Their specialization equalities are reflexivity lemmas, so all normalization of these constructors takes place in the abstract categorical proof.

proof_origin.note: E3: complete Lean proof using the already proved exact-derived square-pasting theorem. Generic restriction_path and explicit ordinary/bounded-below square expansion equations avoid expensive concrete conversion. All private helpers are proved; no new obligations or public interface changes.

lean.statement:
theorem comparisonSquareEtalePath_normalization
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (M : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))) :
    HEq
      (comparisonSquareDerivedPath Λ g' f' f g (comparisonSquareEtalePath Λ
        { toCommSq := sq.toCommSq, isoPullback := sq.isoPullback,
          hom_fst := sq.isoPullback_hom_fst, hom_snd := sq.isoPullback_hom_snd }) M)
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.ι ⋙ D(ν^*(X')[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])).map
            ((Etale.pullbackSquareComparison (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) sq.toCommSq).hom.app M) ≫
          (leftDerivedUpperStarComparisonIso g' Λ).hom.app
            (D+(Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).obj M) ≫
          L(ProEtale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) g').map
            ((leftDerivedUpperStarComparisonIso f Λ).hom.app M))
